requirements: The core contributions of the XGrammar paper — an adaptive-token-mask-cache-based structured-generation engine that achieves up to 100× speedup for CFG mask generation and near-zero overhead in end-to-end LLM serving — have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The two PDA structure optimizations from Section 3.4 — fragment-rule inlining (bounded-size, iterated) and node merging (same-label successors and epsilon-edge collapsing) — are implemented while preserving equivalence.
Fragment-rule inlining (Section 3.4) is implemented as a bounded, iterated PDA transformation that folds terminal-only fragment rules into their parent rules.

Code has been implemented that defines a `RuleInliner` (or equivalent) pass over the byte-level PDA/CFG intermediate representation with an entry point that takes the PDA and returns a semantically equivalent PDA with fragment rules inlined.

verification.spec: Use importlib to import the RuleInliner (or equivalent named) class/function; assert it exposes a callable entry point that accepts a PDA/CFG IR and returns a PDA of the same type. Check signature via inspect.signature.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that identifies inlining-eligible fragment rules as those whose FSA contains no rule-reference edges (only character edges), matching the paper's `rules that do not reference other rules` criterion in Section 3.4.

verification.spec: Construct a small grammar with (i) a fragment rule containing only character edges and (ii) a rule that references another rule. Call the eligibility predicate on both; assert (i) is eligible for inlining and (ii) is not.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces the paper's `limit the size of the inlined rule and the size of the inlined result to constants` bound, exposing two configurable size constants and skipping any inlining that would exceed them.

verification.spec: Verify two configurable constants (max_inlined_rule_size and max_inlined_result_size) exist on the inliner API. Create a fragment rule that would exceed the result-size bound and assert it is NOT inlined; create one under the bound and assert it IS inlined.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that iterates the inlining pass until a fixpoint (no further eligible fragment rule is picked) rather than performing a single sweep.

verification.spec: Build a chain of fragment rules A->B->C where each references the next but none references any rule outside the chain. After a single call to the top-level inline pass, assert all three are inlined into their parents (fixpoint reached) rather than only one level being resolved.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test has been implemented on a small synthetic CFG with several trivial fragment rules that shows the inlining pass replaces all references to those rules with their expanded character sequences and removes the rules from the rule set.

verification.spec: Run the unit test that constructs a synthetic CFG with several trivial fragment rules (e.g., DIGIT ::= '0'|'1'|..., WS ::= ' ') referenced in a parent rule; after inlining, assert (a) rule set no longer contains DIGIT/WS and (b) parent rule's FSA has the character sequences expanded inline.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral equivalence test has been implemented that fuzzes strings against the pre-inlining PDA and post-inlining PDA and asserts they accept/reject the same set of strings.

verification.spec: Generate ~1000 random strings (including edge cases: empty, long, boundary-adjacent). Feed each to both the pre-inlining PDA and post-inlining PDA; assert accept/reject decisions match on every input.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test has been implemented showing that on the JSON grammar used in the paper, iterated inlining reduces the count of fragment rules (rules with no rule-references and size below the bound) to near zero, matching the paper's claim that inlining `almost eliminated fragment rules`.

verification.spec: Load the JSON grammar used in the paper, apply iterated inlining, then count remaining fragment rules (rules with no rule-references and size <= bound). Assert count is <= 2 (near zero), matching the paper's 'almost eliminated' claim.

sub_tasks.requirements: Node merging for same-label successor edges (Section 3.4) is implemented on the PDA graph.

Code has been implemented that scans every PDA node for pairs of outward edges that share the same label (byte, byte class, or rule reference) and enumerates the corresponding successor pairs as merge candidates.

verification.spec: Construct a PDA node with two outward edges sharing the same label to distinct successors, plus a third edge with a different label. Call the merge-candidate enumerator and assert it returns the two same-label successors as a candidate pair and not the third.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that only merges same-label successors when they satisfy both conditions from Section 3.4: (a) they are pointed to by edges with the same label originating from the same source node, and (b) they have no other incoming edges from elsewhere in the automaton.

verification.spec: Build two test cases: (case A) node with two same-label edges to successors that have no other incoming edges - assert merge occurs; (case B) same setup but one successor also has an incoming edge from a different source node - assert merge is refused.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, after merging, rewrites all outward edges of the merged successors onto the surviving node and removes the redundant duplicate edge, keeping the PDA well-formed (no dangling references).

verification.spec: After node merging, iterate over all edges of the resulting PDA and assert (a) no edge references a removed node id, (b) both mergees' outward edges appear on the surviving node, (c) exactly one edge remains for the previously duplicated label from the source.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test has been implemented on a hand-built PDA with a node exposing two identical-label outward edges to distinct successors, asserting the merger produces a single successor and that string acceptance is preserved.

verification.spec: Run the unit test: hand-build a PDA with node N having two 'a'-labeled edges to distinct successors S1 and S2; call the merger; assert (a) result has a single successor after 'a' from N, (b) accepting strings that used to reach either S1 or S2 still accept.

sub_tasks.requirements: Epsilon-edge collapsing under the paper's constraints (Section 3.4) is implemented as a node-merging pass.
Code has been implemented that identifies epsilon edges (s -epsilon-> t) in the PDA, distinct from character or rule-reference edges.

verification.spec: Construct a PDA containing an epsilon edge (or a mix of epsilon, character, and rule-reference edges). Call the epsilon-identification helper; assert it returns exactly the epsilon edges and none of the character or rule-reference edges.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that collapses an epsilon edge s -epsilon-> t only when either (a) s has no other outward edge, or (b) t has no other inward edge, matching the disjunctive condition in Section 3.4.

verification.spec: Build three PDAs: (i) s has only the epsilon edge -> collapse expected, (ii) t has only one inward edge (the epsilon) -> collapse expected, (iii) s has multiple outward AND t has multiple inward -> collapse refused. Assert the collapse function behaves accordingly.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, after merging s and t, splices the outward edges of t onto the merged node and rewires all inward edges of t/s to the merged node without introducing self-loops from the collapsed epsilon.

verification.spec: After collapsing s -epsilon-> t, assert (a) the merged node contains all of t's outward edges, (b) all edges previously pointing to s or t now point to the merged node, (c) no self-loops introduced from the collapsed epsilon edge itself.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test has been implemented that verifies an epsilon edge whose source has a second outward transition AND whose target has a second inward transition is NOT collapsed, protecting the negative case in Section 3.4's rule.

verification.spec: Construct a PDA where s -epsilon-> t, s has a second outward edge to a distinct node, AND t has a second inward edge from a different node. Call the epsilon-collapse pass; assert the epsilon edge is preserved (not collapsed) and the PDA is unchanged.

sub_tasks.requirements: The two structure optimizations are wired into the PDA build pipeline and demonstrably reduce the automaton size while preserving semantics.

Code has been implemented that runs rule inlining and both node-merging optimizations as an ordered pipeline invoked from the PDA construction path, with a flag to enable/disable each pass for ablation.

verification.spec: Invoke PDA construction with all combinations of enable_inlining and enable_node_merging flags (four combos). Verify (a) each combo produces a valid PDA, (b) node/edge counts differ between combos, (c) the pipeline invokes inlining before node merging (order preserved).

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test on the JSON grammar has been implemented that reports the number of PDA nodes and edges before and after applying the two optimizations and asserts both counts strictly decrease, matching Section 3.4's claim that the optimizations reduce the number of nodes and edges.

verification.spec: Load the JSON CFG, build a PDA without optimizations (record #nodes, #edges), then rebuild with rule inlining + both node-merging cases enabled (record #nodes, #edges). Assert optimized_nodes < baseline_nodes AND optimized_edges < baseline_edges.

sub_tasks.requirements: A property-based / random-string equivalence test has been implemented that confirms the fully-optimized PDA (inlining + both node-merging cases) accepts exactly the same language as the unoptimized PDA for the JSON, XML and Python DSL grammars used in Section 4.

verification.spec: For each of JSON, XML, and Python DSL grammars used in Section 4, generate ~500 random strings (mix of valid samples produced from the grammar and adversarial invalid strings). Feed to unoptimized and fully-optimized PDA; assert identical accept/reject decisions on every string.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test has been implemented showing that when context expansion (Section 3.2) is combined with fragment-rule inlining, the number of context-dependent tokens on the Llama-3.1 / JSON pipeline decreases relative to running context expansion alone, confirming the interaction described in Section 3.4 where inlining `enhances the effectiveness of context expansion`.

verification.spec: On the JSON grammar with the Llama-3.1 tokenizer, count context-dependent tokens after: (a) context expansion only, and (b) context expansion + fragment-rule inlining. Assert (b) < (a), confirming inlining reduces context-dependent token count when combined with context expansion.

sub_tasks.requirements: Quantitative claims (from Section 3.4 / Table 3) about the standalone speedups of these two structural optimizations are reproduced under the paper's measurement conditions.

A measurement script has been implemented that, on the CFG (unconstrained JSON) task with Llama-3.1-8B and the json-mode-eval dataset, records average per-token mask-generation latency for (a) the PDA baseline (no optimizations) and (b) baseline + node merging only, and reports the ratio.

verification.spec: Execute the measurement script on the CFG (unconstrained JSON) task with Llama-3.1-8B tokenizer and the json-mode-eval dataset. Verify it emits average per-token mask-generation latency for two configurations: (a) PDA baseline, (b) baseline + node merging, and prints the ratio.

sub_tasks.requirements: Reproduced measurement matches the paper's Table 3 claim (claim 15) that adding node merging on top of the PDA baseline reduces per-token latency from 65.776 ms to 38.280 ms (a 1.7x speedup) within tolerance.

verification.spec: Run the ablation measurement on the CFG (unconstrained JSON) / Llama-3.1-8B / json-mode-eval benchmark. Compute the speedup ratio between PDA baseline (paper: 65.776 ms) and baseline + node merging (paper: 38.280 ms). Assert measured ratio is 1.7x within tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: A measurement script has been implemented that, holding node merging and the adaptive token mask cache enabled, measures per-token mask-generation latency with and without rule inlining on the same CFG (unconstrained JSON) / Llama-3.1-8B benchmark.

verification.spec: Execute the measurement script that fixes node-merging + adaptive-token-mask-cache to enabled and toggles rule inlining. Verify it produces two latency numbers (with/without inlining) on the CFG (unconstrained JSON) / Llama-3.1-8B / json-mode-eval benchmark and reports the ratio.

sub_tasks.requirements: Reproduced measurement matches the paper's Table 3 claim (claim 16) that adding rule inlining on top of node merging + adaptive token mask cache reduces per-token latency from 0.154 ms to 0.035 ms (a 4.4x speedup) within tolerance.

verification.spec: Run the rule-inlining ablation measurement (baseline: node merging + adaptive token mask cache = 0.154 ms; +rule inlining = 0.035 ms). Compute the speedup ratio and assert measured value is 4.4x within tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The mask-generation / LLM-inference overlap from Section 3.5 is implemented: mask-cache build overlaps with prefill, per-token mask generation overlaps with decoding, and a sync-before-sampling barrier feeds the mask into masked sampling on the GPU.
CPU-side mask generation is decoupled from the GPU inference path so it can run concurrently with LLM prefill/decode.
Code has been implemented that spawns a CPU-side mask-generation worker (thread, futures/executor, or async task) which the LLM engine can dispatch to without blocking the GPU-side forward pass.

verification.spec: Import the engine module and verify that a CPU-side mask-generation worker exists as a thread, concurrent.futures.Executor, or asyncio task. Inspect the engine's decode/dispatch code and assert that mask_generate() is submitted to this worker (e.g. executor.submit / threading.Thread / loop.create_task) rather than called synchronously inline before the GPU forward.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the mask-generation worker's inputs are only the previously generated tokens and the PDA/mask-cache state; it never reads GPU tensors, hidden states, or logits, matching Section 3.5's premise that CPU mask gen depends only on prior tokens.

verification.spec: Instantiate the mask-generation worker with a mock/stub GPU inference module that raises on any tensor read. Feed a fixed prior-token sequence and PDA state and verify the worker produces a mask without accessing GPU tensors, hidden states, or logits. Inspect worker signature/inputs and assert no GPU handles are passed.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that running the mask-generation worker on a fixed prior-token sequence deterministically produces the same mask when the GPU inference path is stubbed out or replaced, confirming CPU-only dependency.

verification.spec: Run pytest on a unit test that stubs the GPU inference path (e.g. replaces logits computation with a no-op), calls the mask-gen worker twice on identical prior-token sequences, and asserts the two returned masks are bitwise-equal, confirming deterministic CPU-only mask generation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Mask-cache preprocessing (context-independent token precomputation) is scheduled to overlap with LLM prefill of the prompt, as depicted in Figure 8.

Code has been implemented so that when a new grammar-constrained request enters the engine, mask-cache construction (adaptive token mask cache preprocessing) is dispatched to the CPU worker at the same time the prefill kernel is launched on the GPU.

verification.spec: Submit a grammar-constrained request to the engine with instrumented start-timestamps for (a) mask-cache preprocessing and (b) prefill kernel launch. Assert both are initiated within a small window (e.g. < 5 ms) of each other and that the mask-cache build runs on a distinct thread/executor from the prefill call.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test measures the wall-clock time of (prefill+mask-cache-build) with overlap enabled and confirms it is strictly less than the sum of prefill-only time plus mask-cache-build-only time, demonstrating actual overlap rather than serialization.

verification.spec: Measure wall-clock T_overlap for (prefill + mask-cache-build) with overlap enabled; T_prefill for prefill-only (grammar disabled); T_mask for mask-cache-build only (no prefill). Assert T_overlap < T_prefill + T_mask - epsilon (e.g. at least 10% savings), demonstrating actual concurrent execution.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-token mask generation runs concurrently with the GPU decoding step, per Figure 8.

Code has been implemented so that at each decoding iteration the engine issues the CPU mask-gen call for step t+1 immediately after the token from step t is available, so that mask gen for step t+1 runs during the GPU forward pass of step t+1.

verification.spec: Instrument the decode loop to log per-step timestamps for token-sampled-at-step-t and mask-gen-dispatched-for-step-t+1. Assert mask-gen dispatch for step t+1 occurs immediately (< 1 ms) after token t is sampled and before the GPU forward for step t+1 finishes.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test with an instrumented decode loop records timestamps for (a) GPU-forward-start/end and (b) CPU-mask-gen-start/end and asserts their intervals overlap for at least the first several decoding steps under a JSON-schema constraint.

verification.spec: Run a decode of at least 8 steps under a JSON schema constraint with instrumentation that records GPU-forward-start/end and CPU-mask-gen-start/end. Assert that for at least 3 of the first 5 decoding steps the GPU and CPU intervals overlap in time (i.e. mask_gen_start < gpu_end and gpu_start < mask_gen_end).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that after each sampled token updates the PDA persistent-execution-stack state on the CPU so the next mask-gen call reflects the newly generated token, matching the feedback loop in Section 3.5.

verification.spec: Sample a sequence of tokens under a JSON constraint and inspect the persistent execution stack after each step. Assert the stack top advances to reflect the newly-sampled token before the next mask-gen call is made (e.g. call accept_token(t) then verify next mask reflects the post-t state).

sub_tasks.requirements: A sync-before-sampling barrier ensures the CPU-generated mask is available on the GPU before masked sampling is performed.

Code has been implemented with an explicit synchronization primitive (join / future.wait / event) that the sampling kernel waits on before it consumes the mask, so sampling cannot proceed with a stale or missing mask.

verification.spec: Inspect the sampling code path and confirm the presence of an explicit sync primitive (Future.result(), Thread.join(), Event.wait(), asyncio.await, or CUDA event) that the sampler awaits before reading the mask. A unit test attempts sampling before the mask future resolves and asserts it blocks (or raises) rather than proceeding.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that transfers the CPU-generated per-token bitmask to the GPU (as a bool/int tensor of vocabulary size) before sampling, adding -inf to logits at rejected positions.

verification.spec: Call the mask-application function with a fake logits tensor on GPU and a known bitmask. Assert positions where mask==0 have logits set to -inf (or a large negative number) and positions where mask==1 are unchanged. Verify the bitmask tensor is placed on the GPU (torch device is cuda) and its length equals vocabulary size.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test injects a delayed mask-gen callback and verifies that sampling blocks until the mask arrives (rather than sampling from unmasked logits), confirming the barrier is actually load-bearing.

verification.spec: Inject a mask-gen callback that sleeps for 500 ms. Time the sampling call and assert it blocks for at least ~500 ms (indicating the barrier waited on the mask) and that the token sampled respects the mask, rather than being sampled from unmasked logits.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test confirms that after masked sampling, only tokens whose mask bit is 1 can be sampled: over 1000 sampling calls with a restrictive mask, no rejected token id is ever produced.

verification.spec: Construct a restrictive bitmask allowing only 5 out of the vocabulary of >100K tokens. Sample 1000 tokens under this mask from arbitrary logits distributions. Assert every sampled token id belongs to the 5 allowed ids and no rejected id is ever produced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The overlap mechanism is wired into the two LLM serving engines used in Section 4.2 (MLC-LLM and SGLang) so end-to-end runs actually exercise it.

Code has been implemented that registers the CPU mask-gen worker with the MLC-LLM engine's decoding loop so mask gen is launched alongside the prefill/decoding CUDA streams rather than inline before sampling.

verification.spec: Locate the MLC-LLM integration code and verify that the CPU mask-gen worker is registered as a hook (e.g. before-sample callback or dispatch queue) that runs concurrently with prefill/decode CUDA streams, not inline before sampling. Inspect the registration site and confirm the worker is launched via executor/thread before the CUDA sync point.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that installs the XGrammar mask-gen callback into SGLang's per-request scheduler so per-token masks are produced concurrently with SGLang's decode step and consumed at its sampler.

verification.spec: Locate the SGLang integration and confirm the XGrammar mask-gen callback is registered with SGLang's per-request scheduler (e.g. via scheduler hook or logits processor plugin). Inspect the code path and verify per-token masks are produced asynchronously with SGLang's decode step and consumed at its sampler.

sub_tasks.requirements: The overlap achieves the near-zero-overhead TPOT claim from Table 2 on the MLC-LLM engine with Llama-3.1-8B (JSON Schema and CFG(JSON), batch sizes 1 and 16).
The measured TPOT delta between 'with XGrammar' and 'without XGrammar' on MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B for the JSON Schema task at batch size 1 is near zero (paper reports 6.2 vs 6.3 ms; overhead ≈0.1 ms).

verification.spec: From the Table 2 reproduction, extract TPOT with XGrammar minus TPOT without XGrammar for MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B on JSON Schema at batch size 1. Paper reports 6.3 - 6.2 = 0.1 ms overhead.

sub_tasks.requirements: The measured TPOT delta between 'with XGrammar' and 'without XGrammar' on MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B for the JSON Schema task at batch size 16 is near zero (paper reports 9.0 vs 9.2 ms; overhead ≈0.2 ms).

verification.spec: From the Table 2 reproduction, extract TPOT with XGrammar minus TPOT without XGrammar for MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B on JSON Schema at batch size 16. Paper reports 9.2 - 9.0 = 0.2 ms overhead.

sub_tasks.requirements: The measured TPOT delta between 'with XGrammar' and 'without XGrammar' on MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B for the CFG (JSON) task at batch size 1 is near zero (paper reports 6.3 vs 6.3 ms; overhead ≈0.0 ms).

verification.spec: From the Table 2 reproduction, extract TPOT with XGrammar minus TPOT without XGrammar for MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B on CFG (unconstrained JSON) at batch size 1. Paper reports 6.3 - 6.3 = 0.0 ms overhead.

sub_tasks.requirements: The measured TPOT delta between 'with XGrammar' and 'without XGrammar' on MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B for the CFG (JSON) task at batch size 16 is near zero (paper reports 9.0 vs 9.1 ms; overhead ≈0.1 ms).

verification.spec: From the Table 2 reproduction, extract TPOT with XGrammar minus TPOT without XGrammar for MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B on CFG (unconstrained JSON) at batch size 16. Paper reports 9.1 - 9.0 = 0.1 ms overhead.

sub_tasks.requirements: A regression test measures TPOT with the overlap mechanism artificially disabled (mask gen forced to run serially before sampling) and confirms TPOT increases meaningfully, showing that the near-zero-overhead result in Table 2 is attributable to the overlap and not to mask gen simply being fast.

verification.spec: Add a config flag `disable_overlap` that forces mask-gen to run synchronously before sampling. Measure TPOT with overlap enabled vs disabled on MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B for JSON Schema at batch size 1. Assert the disabled TPOT exceeds the enabled TPOT by a meaningful margin (e.g. at least 5% or 0.3 ms), confirming Table 2's near-zero overhead is due to overlap.

sub_tasks.requirements: The baseline constrained-decoding libraries used in Section 4 (Outlines v1.0, llama.cpp b3998 built-in grammar engine, lm-format-enforcer v0.10.9) are installed at the specified versions and wired into a common measurement harness for JSON Schema, unconstrained-JSON CFG, XML CFG, and Python-DSL CFG.
Outlines v1.0 is installed and wrapped for use as a per-token mask generation baseline covering JSON Schema and the paper's three CFG tasks.

Code has been implemented that installs Outlines pinned to version 1.0 (e.g. `outlines==1.0` in `requirements.txt`/`pyproject.toml` or an equivalent pip install command in `setup.sh`) and the installed version is verifiable at runtime via `outlines.__version__` or `pip show outlines`.

verification.spec: Inspect `requirements.txt`/`pyproject.toml`/`setup.sh` for a pin like `outlines==1.0`. Run `pip show outlines` in the environment and assert Version == 1.0. Also import outlines and check `outlines.__version__ == '1.0'`.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that wraps Outlines behind a `MaskGenerator` interface with methods to (a) accept a JSON Schema, an unconstrained-JSON CFG, an XML CFG, or a Python-DSL CFG and (b) return the token-level accept mask for a given prior output prefix on the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct tokenizer.

verification.spec: Instantiate the MaskGenerator wrapper around Outlines. Verify it accepts each of {JSON Schema, unconstrained JSON CFG, XML CFG, Python-DSL CFG} via its constructor and exposes a method that, given a prior-output prefix, returns the token accept mask against the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct tokenizer. Test all four grammar types with a small prefix and assert mask output is well-formed.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Outlines wrapper deterministically returns a mask vector whose length equals the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct vocabulary size (128256) and whose entries are 0/1 (or -inf/0 logit bias) for a fixed prefix input, verifiable by a unit test that fixes the prefix and asserts mask-length and dtype.

verification.spec: Fix a JSON Schema and a prefix such as '{'. Call the Outlines wrapper's mask method and assert (a) len(mask) == 128256 (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct vocab size), (b) mask.dtype is bool or int (0/1) or float (-inf/0 logit bias), and (c) calling it twice on the same input returns identical arrays.

sub_tasks.requirements: The llama.cpp grammar engine at build b3998 is compiled and wrapped so it can produce per-token constrained-decoding masks for JSON Schema and the paper's three CFGs.

Code has been implemented that checks out and builds the llama.cpp repository at the exact tag/commit `b3998` (e.g. via `git checkout b3998 && make` in a build script) and the resulting binary/library reports build tag b3998 in its logs or `--version` output.

verification.spec: Run the build script that clones llama.cpp and runs `git checkout b3998 && make`. Verify `git rev-parse HEAD` inside the cloned repo resolves to tag b3998 (or the corresponding commit), and that the resulting `main`/`llama-cli` binary reports build tag b3998 in its `--version` output or startup log.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that converts each of the paper's grammars (JSON Schema, unconstrained JSON, XML 1.0, Python DSL) into the GBNF grammar format that llama.cpp's built-in grammar engine expects, with converter functions callable from the harness.

verification.spec: Import the converter module. For each of {JSON Schema, unconstrained JSON, XML 1.0, Python DSL}, call the converter and obtain a GBNF grammar string. Feed each GBNF into llama.cpp's grammar parser (e.g. `llama_grammar_init` via bindings or CLI `--grammar`) and assert parsing succeeds without error for all four.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that wraps the llama.cpp grammar engine (via Python bindings such as `llama-cpp-python` pinned to a b3998-compatible version, or via the C API through ctypes) so it exposes the same `MaskGenerator` interface as the Outlines wrapper and returns a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-sized token mask per call.

verification.spec: Import the llama.cpp wrapper module and instantiate its MaskGenerator subclass. Confirm it exposes prepare(grammar) and next_mask(prefix_token_ids) methods, that next_mask returns a boolean/int mask of length equal to the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct vocabulary (~128256), and that the underlying binding version corresponds to llama.cpp b3998 (check bindings metadata or a version string).

sub_tasks.requirements: lm-format-enforcer v0.10.9 is installed and wrapped as a regex-based baseline that is applied only to JSON Schema (and omitted for the CFG tasks it cannot express).
Code has been implemented that installs lm-format-enforcer pinned to version 0.10.9 (e.g. `lm-format-enforcer==0.10.9`) and the installed version is verifiable via `pip show lm-format-enforcer`.

verification.spec: Run `pip show lm-format-enforcer` in the reproduction environment and assert the reported Version is exactly 0.10.9. Also assert `import lmformatenforcer; lmformatenforcer.__version__ == '0.10.9'`.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that wraps lm-format-enforcer behind the shared `MaskGenerator` interface for JSON Schema inputs on the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct tokenizer, producing a full-vocab token mask per call.

verification.spec: Instantiate the lm-format-enforcer adapter subclass of MaskGenerator with a small JSON schema and the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct tokenizer. Call prepare(schema) then next_mask([]) and assert the returned mask has length == tokenizer.vocab_size (~128256) and contains at least one True and at least one False entry.

sub_tasks.requirements: The harness explicitly marks lm-format-enforcer as unsupported for the unconstrained-JSON, XML, and Python-DSL CFG tasks and skips it in the results table with a `not applicable` marker rather than reporting fabricated numbers, matching the paper's Figure 9 layout that omits lm-format-enforcer from all three CFG panels.

verification.spec: Run the microbenchmark harness across all six (backend, task) combinations. Inspect the results file (e.g., results/mask_latency.json): assert that entries for lm-format-enforcer on tasks 'cfg_unconstrained_json', 'cfg_xml', 'cfg_python_dsl' exist with a sentinel value like 'N/A' or null (not a numeric latency).

sub_tasks.requirements: A shared measurement harness is implemented that drives all three baseline wrappers and XGrammar under identical conditions across the JSON Schema, unconstrained-JSON, XML, and Python-DSL tasks used in Figures 9 and 10.

Code has been implemented that defines a single `MaskGenerator` abstract interface (or equivalent protocol) with `prepare(grammar)` and `next_mask(prefix_token_ids) -> mask` methods, and all four backends (Outlines, llama.cpp, lm-format-enforcer, XGrammar) subclass it so the harness is grammar-library-agnostic.

verification.spec: Import the MaskGenerator base class and all four adapter classes (Outlines, llama.cpp, lm-format-enforcer, XGrammar). Assert each is a subclass of MaskGenerator and defines prepare(grammar) and next_mask(prefix_token_ids) methods via inspect.signature.

verification.spec: Instantiate the persistent stack; push shared prefix, then branch into 3 divergent stacks; assert deep-node objects are shared by identity (id()) across branches (structural sharing); perform 100 push/pop cycles then roll back to a saved handle and assert stack state matches the saved snapshot; measure that rollback runtime is independent of stack depth

verification.spec: Import the persistent stack module; construct a stack with depth D=1000 shared prefix; branch it K=50 times via the branch/split API; assert (a) all K resulting stack handles reference the same shared prefix nodes (identity check on internal node pointers) and (b) the wall-clock time per branch is O(1), i.e. does not scale with D (branch time at D=1000 within 3x of branch time at D=10)
verification.paper_cite: Section 3.3, 'we only need to split the branch for that stack instead of copying the whole stack'

verification.spec: Instantiate the persistent stack with a history window size W; advance the stack by W+5 tokens; assert that (a) rolling back up to W steps returns the stack top pointer to the exact prior state (top-node identity match) and (b) rolling back further than W raises or returns a sentinel indicating history is unavailable
verification.paper_cite: Section 3.3, 'a sliding window of history is maintained'

sub_tasks.requirements: Method components (from critique splits and additions)

Code has been implemented and run such that the pushdown automaton definition in Appendix A is realized: XGrammar's PDA exposes a finite set of grammar rules R and a byte-level input alphabet Σ used at construction time

verification.spec: Import PDA construction module; instantiate PDA on a small grammar; assert PDA object exposes attributes/methods enumerating rule set R (list of grammar rules) and input alphabet Σ (byte range 0-255)
verification.paper_cite: Appendix A formal PDA definition (tuple with R, Σ)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that for each rule r in R, the corresponding finite-state automaton A_r is materialized with its finite state set Q_r and start state q_r^start (Appendix A definition)

verification.spec: Construct PDA for a two-rule grammar; for each rule r retrieve the per-rule FSA A_r; assert Q_r is a non-empty finite set and q_r^start is in Q_r
verification.paper_cite: Appendix A ('For each rule r ∈ R, the corresponding finite state automaton is given by...')

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the PDA state set Q is defined as the union of all per-rule FSA state sets and the initial PDA state is q_0 = q_main^start (Appendix A)

verification.spec: Construct PDA; assert PDA.states == union(A_r.states for r in R) and PDA.initial_state == A_main.start_state
verification.paper_cite: Appendix A ('the state set Q is defined as the union of all states from the FSAs... initial state to be q_0 = q_main^start')

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that character transitions δ_r in per-rule FSAs are lifted to PDA transitions δ' that consume the character and advance the top-of-stack state (Appendix A construction)

verification.spec: Construct PDA for grammar with a character-only rule ('a' 'b'); step PDA with byte 'a' then 'b'; assert stack-top advances through the two states without any push/pop
verification.paper_cite: Appendix A ('For each character transition in some δ_r ...')

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that for each character-transition inclusion, δ' contains the corresponding lifted transition preserving source/destination (Appendix A: 'we include in δ' the transition ...')

verification.spec: Construct PDA; for a rule with N character edges, assert |δ'_character| == N and each edge preserves its (src, char, dst) triple relative to the source FSA
verification.paper_cite: Appendix A construction of δ' from δ_r character transitions

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that rule-reference transitions in δ_r are simulated by ε-transitions in the PDA that push return information and transfer control to the called rule (Appendix A)

verification.spec: Construct PDA on a grammar with rule ref (main -> <sub>; sub -> 'x'); step PDA from initial state without consuming a byte; assert an ε-transition fires that pushes a return frame and sets stack-top to sub's start state
verification.paper_cite: Appendix A ('For each rule reference transition in δ_r, ... we simulate the recursive call by defining an ε-transition')

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the ε-transition for a rule call pushes (r, q') return information where q ∈ A_r and (r, q') identifies the resume point after the callee returns (Appendix A formal definition)

verification.spec: Construct PDA with main -> <sub> 'y'; inspect the ε-transition for the rule ref; assert its push payload equals (main, q_after_ref) where q_after_ref is the state in A_main reached after the ref edge
verification.paper_cite: Appendix A ('where q belongs to the automaton A_r, and (r, q') ...')

verification.spec: Run harness.run_mlc(model='Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct', dataset='json-mode-eval', task='json_schema', batch_size=1, xgrammar=True) on an NVIDIA H100; record TPOT_ms; assert |TPOT_ms - 6.3| / 6.3 <= 0.20; also run xgrammar=False variant and assert both TPOT values are recorded to results/

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the end-to-end harness sweeps batch sizes 1 and 16 for the JSON schema task with XGrammar enabled on MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B, and the measured TPOT at batch=16 matches the paper's 9.2 ms/token within tolerance

verification.spec: Run harness with batch_size sweep [1, 16] on JSON schema task; assert results contain both batch entries; take the batch=16 XGrammar-enabled TPOT_ms and assert |TPOT_ms - 9.2| / 9.2 <= 0.25

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the harness records CFG(unconstrained JSON) TPOT for both XGrammar-enabled and XGrammar-disabled at batch sizes 1 and 16 on MLC-LLM + Llama-3.1-8B, and the measured CFG(JSON) batch=16 XGrammar-enabled TPOT matches the paper's 9.1 ms/token within tolerance

verification.spec: Run harness.run_mlc for task='cfg_json' with (xgrammar in {True, False}) x (batch_size in {1, 16}) yielding four TPOT numbers written to results/tpot_cfg.json; then assert |TPOT[xgrammar=True,batch=16] - 9.1| / 9.1 <= 0.25
